svg.aria-label: How towonel-operator works: Gateways, HTTPRoutes and Services annotated in a Kubernetes cluster are watched by towonel-operator, which turns each source into a TowonelAgent and manages a TowonelTunnel; the operator registers invites, hostnames and ports with the Towonel Hub and renders towonel-agent Deployments that authenticate with the invite token the hub issues and dial out over QUIC to regional edges (edge-na and edge-eu), where browsers and apps connect over HTTPS and are routed by SNI back through the tunnel to the origin Service. Nothing listens on the home network.
svg.text: Annotate a Route, Get a Public Hostname: Kubernetes In, Towonel Out
Sources in your cluster become Towonel tunnels and agents; the hub authorizes hostnames and the edge carries traffic home.

text.tspan: • TowonelTunnel owns the invite, the token Secret
• Authorizes each hostname for one invite.
• Open the public hostname over HTTPS, from anywhere.
• Dial out over QUIC; no inbound ports.
• Routes by SNI to the tunnel that owns the hostname.

svg.text: Nothing listens on your network: agents dial out, the edge brings the traffic back.
